A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same BlendRL work, with complete main texts and appendices. Equations, figures, tables and retained experiments can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Atari training results, modified-environment evaluations, policy-interaction analyses and a neural-versus-logic blending ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds object-detection noise experiments, explanation case studies, action-distribution measurements and rule-generation trials.

M1.justification: The blended policy, mixed critic, PPO training and entropy regularizer remain unchanged. Beyond v1's rule-derived interpretations, v2 adds LLM postprocessing that generates narrative explanations from task descriptions, logical facts and selected actions (A.15).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Kangaroo, Seaquest and DonkeyKong and retain the original environmental modifications. v2 adds test scenarios with randomly missing detected objects (A.11), extending input-condition coverage without adding game benchmarks.

E2.justification: The comparison expands from PPO and NUDGE to include DQN, NLRL, SCoBots and INTERPRETER across the three games, plus INSIGHT on Seaquest (v2 Tables 1 and 3). v2 combines conducted experiments, previously reported baseline scores and extended evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 adds human-normalized scores, test-only object masking at probabilities 0.1–0.5 evaluated over 10 episodes, a 10,000-step action-distribution analysis, and controlled rule-generation tests with policy-equivalence success criteria. These substantially expand evaluation procedures; the original training budgets, architectures and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original environmental robustness and blending-module studies remain. v2 adds missing-object sensitivity tests (A.11), attribution comparisons between active policy modes (A.14), action-frequency analysis (A.16), and ablations of rule-example quality and quantity with failure cases (A.17).

E5.justification: v2 adds success-rate estimation over 10 GPT-4o trials for each rule-generation condition (A.17). The original three-seed learning curves and ten-seed robustness/blending reporting remain; the PDFs do not establish increased reruns for those original experiments.

E6.justification: The original learning curves and robustness/blending table values are retained. v2 adds extensive comparator scores and new noise, explanation and action-distribution findings. Table 9 reports 100% rule-generation success with either five optimal or three suboptimal examples, but 0% without examples, across all three games. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal consequence-operator definition and grounding example (A.1.1), plus explicit memory-complexity expressions including parallel environments (A.1.3). The existing reasoning-graph definition, message-passing equations and PPO mathematics are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: joint neural/symbolic policy learning, hybrid PPO optimization, Atari baseline outperformance, robustness and explainability. The expanded experiments primarily change the supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds an important qualification to robustness: missing objects can cause incorrect blending decisions, making accurate object states crucial (A.11). It also interprets attribution complementarity (A.14) and few-shot examples as teaching rule structure rather than strategies (A.17). However, A.16's prose reverses the neural and logic roles displayed in Figure 14.

D1.justification: v1 documents hardware, architectures, hyperparameters and code access but leaves the LLM identity and complete prompts unspecified. v2 identifies GPT-4o and supplies detailed rule-generation, predicate-generation and explanation prompts, including few-shot examples (A.2–A.3 and A.15). This substantially expands reproducibility information without establishing changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds positioning against LTL instruction-following, fast/slow RL and object-centric neural approaches, and revises INSIGHT's description to distinguish distillation and LLM explanations. Several appendix citations to ILP applications are removed. The central positioning around jointly used neural and symbolic policies remains.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording and affiliation/header edits, an ethics statement, expanded forward-reasoning explanations, and appendix reorganization, including moving RL background from A.1 to A.13. Most other expansion accompanies newly documented experiments and technical details.

P2.justification: v2 moves the original learning curves from main-text Figure 5 to appendix Figure 9 and introduces main comparison and raw-score tables. It redraws the reasoning graph, adds a message-passing illustration, and adds noise, attribution and action-distribution figures plus the rule-generation table. Existing displays are largely retained rather than deleted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves empirical scrutiny and reproducibility by broadening the limited PPO/NUDGE comparison, documenting the LLM and prompts, and directly testing perception errors and prompting dependence. These additions address important gaps and expose a consequential robustness limitation. Some added baseline settings remain insufficiently documented, and A.16 contradicts Figure 14, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains.
